title: Slide a quarter sheet pan onto a toaster oven's lower rails, level and all the way in
instruction: Slide the pan onto the toaster oven's lower rails, level and all the way in so the oven door could shut, and take your hands off it.
context: Most adults who cook slide a pan into an oven or toaster oven every week. A sheet pan is carried level by its two short ends, but in a toaster oven the walls stand a few millimetres from those ends and the roof is a few centimetres over the rim, so the hands cannot follow the pan in, and the open drop-down door lies in front of the oven, so the pan is lifted and carried over it: it is set on the rails part way in, let go, and the last stretch is a push on its near rim. A rail must sit under each short end: a pan lowered onto one rail tips, one pushed in askew jams on a side wall, and one left part out stops the door shutting.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +0.305 m and -0.305 m. (1) A fixed countertop toaster oven of the class that takes a quarter sheet pan (about 20 to 25 L; if no oven matches the dimensions here within 3 mm, use a steel or wood box built to them), black painted steel, cold, standing on the table with its open front face (the plane the door shuts against) at x 0.425 m, facing the arms. Outside it is 0.260 m deep (x 0.425 to 0.685), 0.374 m wide and 0.200 m tall. The cavity is 0.344 m wide (y -0.172 to +0.172), 0.245 m deep (the back wall's inner face is at x 0.670 m) and has its floor 0.020 m above the table and its roof 0.190 m above it; the side walls and back wall are 15 mm thick and the roof 10 mm. On each side wall are two pairs of rails (ledges), steel plates 18 mm deep and 4 mm thick running the whole depth: the lower pair with its top at z 0.075 m, the upper pair with its top at z 0.140 m. The rails' inner edges stand 0.308 m apart. The oven's drop-down door is open and lies flat toward the arms, hinged along the front bottom edge of the opening: a steel slab 0.170 m long (x 0.255 to 0.425), 0.374 m wide (y -0.187 to +0.187) and 0.020 m thick, its inner face level with the oven floor (0.020 m above the table), so its free edge is at x 0.255 m. Check with a tape and calipers: cavity width and depth, rail heights, rail spacing, door length and the 3.7 mm front-to-back play of the pan (below), each within 3 mm. (2) A loose standard quarter-size (1/4) sheet pan, bare 18-gauge aluminium, as sold for commercial and home baking, 9-1/2 x 13 x 1 in: 0.241 m deep (x), 0.330 m wide (y), 0.025 m tall, 0.20 kg (a real pan of this size weighs 0.2 to 0.3 kg; record the weight of the one used), with a rolled rim about 16 mm wide round its top edge (check 16 mm, 3 mm either way, with calipers). Bearing check with calipers: the pan rests on the rails by its flat floor, so the floor's outside width across the rails (y) must be 320 to 330 mm (wall taper at most 5 mm a side, so the floor overlaps each rail's inner edge by 6 mm or more; a pan with a narrower floor is not used) and its depth 25 mm, 3 mm either way. The simulated pan has straight walls: its floor is the full 330 x 241 mm. It lies flat on the table with its 0.330 m side along y, centred on y 0, its trailing edge (the rim nearest the arms) at x 0.008 m and its leading edge at x 0.249 m: 6 mm short of the open door's free edge (x 0.255 m) and clear of it, 176 mm short of the oven's face. Grip points: the rolled rim; a person carries it by its two short ends and pushes on its near rim. With the pan on the lower rails its floor edges overlap each rail by 11 mm (6 mm or more for a real pan within the range above) and stand 7 mm from each wall, and its leading edge can touch the back wall; the pan is then 3.7 mm shorter than the cavity is deep. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state read at the last step from the pan's pose and both grippers. On the rails: no corner of the pan's underside more than 3 mm below or 12 mm above the lower rails' top (z 0.075 m), and the pan's edge over each rail's inner edge by 2 mm or more along 50 mm and no corner more than 2 mm inside a wall (so not on the cavity floor, the upper rails or one rail). In: the pan's centre at least 30 mm inside the front face. Level: the pan's floor within 2 degrees of horizontal, face up. Home ("all the way in": it need not touch the back wall): no part of the pan in front of the front face, so the door could shut (the cavity is only 3.7 mm deeper than the pan, so its leading edge is then within 3.7 mm of the back wall). Near: the pan's trailing edge no more than 40 mm in front of the face. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the pan, and over that 1 s the pan is still: it moves under 5 mm and turns under 5 degrees. Score 0 if the pan's lowest point is ever more than 20 mm below the table top (fell off the table), and 0 unless hands off. Otherwise the first rule that holds sets the score, so every end state has one score: 0 unless on the rails and in; 1.0 level and home; 0.5 level, not home, near; 0.25 otherwise (tilted more than 2 degrees, or more than 40 mm out). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. Real trial, per condition: on the rails, a torch along each rail from the front (no short end dropped below the rail top) and a 12 mm block that must not fit under any of the pan's corners; in, a rule from the face to the pan's marked centre line (30 mm); level, a spirit level on the pan floor (2 degrees) or a 12 mm gauge under one short end (2 degrees over 330 mm); home, a straightedge laid across the front face: no part of the pan touches or passes it; near, a rule from the face to the trailing edge (40 mm); hands off, a 30 mm spacer block against each hand and 30 fps video of the last 1 s: no visible motion of the pan against a taped mark on the rail (the 5 mm and 5 degree limits are wider than the eye can see); fall, by eye against a rule.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The pan has straight walls 4 mm thick (real ones taper, about 1 mm) and its rolled rim is a solid 16 x 10 mm bead (est), so the grippers have something to close on. Pan mass 0.20 kg (est) and friction 0.60 static, 0.47 sliding, aluminium on steel. The oven's feet are solid, its rails are 4 mm plates, the open door is a flat solid slab; heating elements, wire rack, glass and controls are omitted ('home' keeps the pan clear of the door's plane). Oven cold, pan empty.
reset_notes: Lay the pan flat on the table, centred on y 0, its 0.330 m side along y and its trailing edge at x 0.008 m (leading edge 6 mm short of the open door's free edge at x 0.255 m). The oven stays where it is, cold, its front face at x 0.425 m, with its door open and lying flat toward the arms. Nothing is consumed; wipe off any grease from earlier runs.
